title: apps/os88ui.inc: the standard controls the KERNEL assembles into itself (OS88UI_KERNEL)
summary: The kernel's copy of os88ui.inc is not one .cold blob: kern_big/kern_mega put 1,089 bytes in .cold, 278 in CTRL.DRV's .modu (the glyph) and 56 in .bss; kern_small puts only the 459-byte scroll bar in .cold, with the button in CTRL.DRV and FDLG.DRV and 42 bytes of .bss; nothing lands in .text. The design and the single-scratch invariant hold. Verified problems: the button fills its interior and letters the caption one or two frame calls later (SPEC 13.14.6 rule 1); os88ovlchk cannot see `%1:` bodies or `section OS88UI_KGLYPH`, so the KBTNIMG/KGLYPH split is safe by inspection only; about 35 resident bytes are free on kern_big with no ABI change (constant kbtn record, the arm_f shim, the dead OS88UI_FILL loads - one of which needs hoisting); and the commentary about the kernel copy was stale in some twenty places, corrected here.

strengths.title: One source, two worlds, through a macro layer rather than a fork
strengths.why: The kernel arm is cheaper than the package arm (UI_ISMONO one cmp; UI_INK a store), the body stays one source, and OS88UI_KFAR gives a block in a module image far primitives without a second body

strengths.title: kern_small pays nothing resident for a button
strengths.why: OS88UI_KBTNIMG expands the button into the only two images that draw one; resident .cold on kern_small holds the scroll bar alone

strengths.title: The .bss rule for kernel scratch is recorded at the point it bites
strengths.why: os88ui_krect's comment carries the sch_isr incident, and every later scratch follows it

strengths.title: The scroll bar is geometry, not policy, with Control-Manager part codes
strengths.why: sbhit returns part codes and leaves action to the caller; the thumb is bordered before it is filled (13.10.5.9)

strengths.title: Meaningless option combinations do not assemble
strengths.why: BIMG, BOWN, NOGLYPH, KGLYPH and others %error in the wrong world

strengths.title: Text is only ever the opaque run
strengths.why: UI_RUN is the only text macro either arm defines; textsites went 3 -> 0 for this file

strengths.title: The single-scratch invariant holds by census
strengths.why: Every writer of os88ui_krect/krec/ksb/armw is a UI-task painter or callback, followed at once by its one consumer
strengths.evidence: kernel/fdlg.inc, files.inc, ctrl.inc, shutdown.inc, hiber.inc (census re-checked by grep)

findings.title: The kernel's standard button fills its interior, frames it, and letters the caption afterwards
findings.detail: OS88UI_BTN_BODY: UI_INK, UI_FILL of the interior, UI_PEN, UI_FRAME, a second UI_FRAME for the default ring, UI_WIDTH, then UI_RUN. Every caption cell is written twice with one or two gfx_frame calls (plus a pen call) between the writes - SPEC.md 13.14.6 rule 1 and the file's own DRAWING RULE 1; os88ui_sbthdraw was reordered for this same interval (13.10.5.9) and the button never was. It runs on every kernel button draw and in every package copy not built OS88UI_BIMG.
findings.recommendation: Pen, frame and ring first; measure and centre the label; then fill the interior and run the caption at once. The kernel arm must bank the [gfx_color] caption ink before the fill's ink store, and CX/DX across the fill. Prove with a fill/run call recorder or m.flicker() on a Disk window header press. Rows: tests/btnall.py, disp*.
findings.bytes_est: +8 to +12 per copy (kern_big/kern_mega .cold resident; kern_small module copies; each package); 0 calls
findings.verify_note: Re-read os88ui.inc:806-911: fill (UI_FILL) precedes UI_PEN, UI_FRAME, the DEF ring UI_FRAME and UI_WIDTH, and UI_RUN comes last; the fill covers the caption cells. Not listed in ABI-BREAK-LIST/KERNEL-BYTE-QUEUE (no os88ui rows); SPEC 20.5.1.3.1 makes the fill unconditional but says nothing about its order, so it is not a deliberate choice. Note the reorder shrinks the interval to zero drawing calls but still writes the caption cells twice (fill then opaque run).

findings.title: os88ovlchk cannot see the KBTNIMG/KGLYPH split it is cited as guarding
findings.detail: (a) OS88UI_BTN_BODY/KBTN_BODY/BHIT_BODY define their routine as a bare `%1:`; LABEL needs a letter first and TLABEL needs `%1 %+ suffix:`, so os88ui_btn/kbtn/bhit and fdb_* never enter the label map and calls to them go untested - on kern_small a resident near call to os88ui_kbtn would pass make. (b) SECT requires `section .\w+`, so `section OS88UI_KGLYPH` is not read and the glyph block is filed under EXTRA's .cold; CPXN hides the panel's legal call. (c) UI_HLINE (`call ct_cw_gfx_hline`, near) has no OS88UI_KFAR arm.
findings.recommendation: Tooling only: let TLABEL accept a bare `%1:`; resolve `section <macro>` through the includer's %define (or a marker) and retire CPXN; give UI_HLINE a KFAR arm or %error it under OS88UI_KFAR. Prove by planting a resident `call os88ui_kbtn` under KERN_SMALL and watching make go red.
findings.verify_note: (a) and (b) confirmed against the regexes at os88ovlchk.py:152/164/189 and the three `%1:` bodies at os88ui.inc:644/1281/6620; ctrl.inc:267-270 itself says CPXN exists because the scan files the glyph as .cold. (c) is half wrong: UI_GRAY is already `call KERNEL_SEG:cw_gfx_fill_gray`, an absolute far call that is correct from any image, so it needs no KFAR arm; only UI_HLINE (near ct_cw_gfx_hline) is a hazard.

findings.title: os88ui_kbtn rebuilds a fully constant one-button record on every call
findings.detail: KBTN_BODY stores BT_RECTS=BX, BT_LABELS, BT_FLAGS, BT_N=1 and BT_DOWN=0 each call; every caller passes BX=os88ui_krect, so all are constant. An initialised record replaces the stores.
findings.recommendation: Make os88ui_krec an initialised .text record {os88ui_krect, os88ui_krlbl, os88ui_krflg, 1, 0, 0}, change kbtn's contract to 'the rect is os88ui_krect', drop the callers' dead `mov bx, os88ui_krect`.
findings.bytes_est: about -28 resident kern_big/kern_mega; kern_small about -4 resident and about -24 in each of CTRL.DRV and FDLG.DRV
findings.verify_note: Every caller's BX is os88ui_krect (fdlg 1108, files 3369, cp_krect 2832 into cp_bemit, sd_rect 237, hbm_btnrect 1109); nothing else writes os88ui_krec; os88ui_btn only reads BT_DOWN. Not in either byte list.

findings.title: os88ui_arm_f is a 4-byte resident .cold shim both callers can do without
findings.detail: Callers are cp_kinit (.text) and the panel's press in CTRL.DRV; both run with DS=KERNEL_SEG and os88ui_armw is .bss, so `mov [os88ui_armw], ax` (3 bytes) replaces `call COLD_SEG:os88ui_arm_f` (5 bytes), as files.inc already writes the word directly.
findings.recommendation: Replace both far calls with the store and delete os88ui_arm_f.
findings.verify_note: os88ui_arm is `mov [os88ui_armw], ax / ret` (os88ui.inc:1804-1806); AX is the value at both sites (xor ax,ax at 329; the press index at 1398); the cp_kinit site is %ifdef KERN_BIG. Byte arithmetic checks.

findings.title: The scroll-bar drag identity (x1,y1) assumes bars cannot share a corner; Disk windows can
findings.detail: os88ui_sbmine identifies the drag's bar by (x1,y1). fm_sbset fills the one block for every Disk window; two with the same right edge and content top share x1,y1 while one hides the other's corner, and a damage repaint of the hidden one mid-drag would run sbfix and draw its thumb at the dragged pos where it is visible.
findings.recommendation: Bank [fm_vp] at the grab and call os88ui_sbfix in fm_sbset only when it matches, or add y2 to the identity.
findings.verify_note: Low and geometric coincidence only, but reachable: files.inc:3356-3361 itself says a damage repaint behind a drag reaches other Disk windows, which is why fm_btn1 tests window identity. SPEC 13.10.5.10's 'cannot share a top-left corner' holds only for two VISIBLE bars.

findings.title: OS88UI_FILL is a dead flag that seven kernel sites still load
findings.detail: The body fills unconditionally; the kernel loads `mov di, OS88UI_FILL` (3 bytes) at seven sites where `xor di, di` (2) would do; fdlg.inc %errors on arithmetic nothing reads; the equ's comment describes it as live.
findings.recommendation: xor di,di at the sites (hoisting the one at ctrl.inc:4302 above `call cpf_vidok`), drop FILL from fdlg.inc's %error, mark the equ historical.
findings.verify_note: Confirmed dead, but not a blind substitution: at ctrl.inc:4302 the load sits between `call cpf_vidok` (returns CF) and `jnc .live`, and `xor di, di` would clobber that CF - that site must move the clear above the call (if cpf_vidok preserves DI) or keep the mov. fdlg_blabel's `inc di` arithmetic still works from 0 (DIS=1, DEF=2). The equ comment is fixed below as a doc fix.

findings.title: 28 bytes of kern_small resident .bss serve only CTRL.DRV and FDLG.DRV
findings.detail: os88ui_krect/krlbl/krflg/krec stay resident on kern_small because the KFAR body reads them through DS=KERNEL_SEG.
findings.bytes_est: -28 resident kern_small if ever done; not proposed
findings.verify_note: fdlg.inc:1289-1291 states the record stays in .bss and is read through DS; spans not re-measured.

findings.title: A full scroll-bar paint greys the track under the thumb before drawing the thumb
findings.detail: os88ui_sbar lays UI_GRAY over the whole track then calls sbthdraw; sub-call interval, and splitting would add a call.
findings.verify_note: Spot-checked: UI_GRAY over the whole track, then sbthumb and sbthdraw.

findings.title: Export the scroll bar (not the button) as appended API cells
findings.detail: The scroll bar is pure geometry over a 7-word block, resident on all three kernels, calling no package code; an appended X-cell family needs no PKG_FMT bump and would save about 500-840 image bytes per bar-using package against about +60 resident per kernel. The button is not a candidate (its gesture calls package near procs).
findings.recommendation: Add as an A-section candidate row so a future 360KB squeeze need not re-derive it; do not take it today.
findings.bytes_est: about +60 resident per kernel; about -500 to -840 per bar-using package image
findings.verify_note: Not listed in ABI-BREAK-LIST.md or KERNEL-BYTE-QUEUE.md (grep for os88ui/kbtn/krect/arm_f: none). Package span figures and the +60 estimate were not re-measured.

doc_fixes.old_text:
`OS88UI_KERNEL` before including it and its six primitive calls become the
kernel's own cold-to-text far calls (`cw_gfx_frame`, `cw_gfx_fill`,
`cw_font_str`, `cw_gfx_pen_cf`, a direct `[gfx_color]` store — and
`font_width` itself, whose shim went in size pass 2 under §2.6.1 because the
body had no near caller of its own); leave it
undefined and they become `OSAPI_GFX_FRAME`, `OSAPI_GFX_FILL`,
`OSAPI_FONT_STR`, `OSAPI_FONT_WIDTH`, `OSAPI_GFX_PEN` and `OSAPI_SET_COLOR`.
Nothing else differs. The kernel includes it **once, into `.cold`**, from
`fdlg.inc`; `ctrl.inc` is cold too and calls it directly, and `apps.inc` is
`.text` and crosses through `os88ui_btn_f`, a `call`/`retf` shim — the
`fdf_`/`cpf_` pattern of §2.6.
doc_fixes.new_text:
`OS88UI_KERNEL` before including it and the button's six primitive calls
become the kernel's own (`ct_cw_gfx_frame`, `ct_cw_gfx_fill`,
`ct_cw_font_run`, `ct_font_width`, `ct_cw_gfx_pen_cf` and a direct
`[gfx_color]` store, or far calls to `KERNEL_SEG:cw_*` and
`KERNEL_SEG:font_width` in a block assembled into an on-demand image); leave
it undefined and they become `OSAPI_GFX_FRAME`, `OSAPI_GFX_FILL`,
`OSAPI_FONT_RUN`, `OSAPI_FONT_WIDTH`, `OSAPI_GFX_PEN` and `OSAPI_SET_COLOR`.
The kernel includes it **once**, from `fdlg.inc`: the button and the scroll
bar land in `.cold`, the glyph in CTRL.DRV's image, and on `kern_small` the
button is expanded into CTRL.DRV and FDLG.DRV instead (§38.0). CTRL.DRV and
HIBER.DRV reach the `.cold` bodies through their own far hops (`CPXC`,
`HBGC`); `os88ui_btn_f`, the `call`/`retf` shim `.text` once crossed through,
went in kernel size pass 15.
doc_fixes.why: The only text primitive is the opaque run (UI_RUN = ct_cw_font_run / OSAPI_FONT_RUN, os88ui.inc:137-143); the kernel arm uses ct_* trampolines (kernel.asm:8098-8108) or KERNEL_SEG far forms under OS88UI_KFAR; the glyph is CTRL.DRV's; ctrl.inc is CTRL.DRV and reaches the bodies through CPXC; apps.inc has no caller and os88ui_btn_f is gone (os88ui.inc:6659-6663).

doc_fixes.old_text:
; SPEC.md 13.10.5.10. There is one gesture record and there are two kernel
; bars, so "a drag is live" and "a drag is live ON THIS BAR" stopped being the
; same question the moment the file dialog was wired. Without this,
; os88ui_sbfix would fix the Disk window's dragged pos into the DIALOG's block
; - a thumb drawn where nothing is, and a hit test that agrees with it.
;
; The identity is (x1, y1), which is enough: two bars on screen at the same
; time cannot share a top-left corner.
doc_fixes.new_text:
; SPEC.md 13.10.5.10. There is one gesture record and one block, and fm_sbset
; fills that block for whichever Disk window is being painted - the file
; dialog's chooser among them - so "a drag is live" and "a drag is live ON THIS
; BAR" are different questions. Without this, os88ui_sbfix would fix the
; dragged window's pos into another window's block - a thumb drawn where
; nothing is, and a hit test that agrees with it.
;
; The identity is (x1, y1): two bars VISIBLE at once cannot share a top-left
; corner. Two Disk windows with the same right edge and content top can, while
; one hides the other's corner, and a damage repaint of the hidden one during
; the drag then takes the dragged pos; the window identity fm_btn1 uses for
; its pressed button would close that.
doc_fixes.why: kernel/fdlg.inc draws no scroll bar (no os88ui_sb reference); fm_sbset (files.inc:3412-3452) is the one setter for every Disk window, two of which can share x1,y1; files.inc:3356-3361 already notes a damage repaint behind a drag reaching another window.
